boundary_decision.rationale: Publication-edition identity composes bibliographic metadata, responsibility statements, issuance mode, seriality, constituent structure, identifier assertions, content bindings, accessibility metadata, rights and market context, lifecycle states, corrections, provenance, preservation bindings, discovery metadata, and standards crosswalks without owning external work, expression, manifestation, asset, copy, party, identifier-agency, publication-workflow, event, rights-instrument, channel, or repository lifecycles. The six-bundle structure (identity/responsibility, issuance/seriality, content/accessibility, identifiers/rights, lifecycle/preservation, discovery/interoperability) demonstrates aggregate composition. The model explicitly refuses work-edition, edition-manifestation, title-as-identity, ISBN-as-universal-identity, and publication-workflow collapse, maintaining IFLA LRM, RDA, and BIBFRAME abstraction boundaries across twenty-four tier-1 sources. Frozen registry value 'standalone-mm' classifies the record plane; subject-model entry kind 'aggregate' is the correct schema enum for the compositional bibliographic edition root.

decisions.concept: Aggregate entry kind for publication-edition composition
decisions.rationale: Edition identity aggregates bibliographic metadata, responsibility, issuance, seriality, identifiers, content bindings, accessibility, rights, lifecycle, preservation, and discovery without absorbing work, expression, asset, party, workflow, or rights-instrument masters. Six-bundle structure is compositionally coherent.

Model refuses to collapse IFLA LRM, RDA, and BIBFRAME abstractions. Work and expression remain external masters. Edition binds but does not own manifestations, assets, copies, or files. Boundary notes across SRC-001, SRC-003, SRC-004 support separation.

decisions.concept: External master declaration for works, parties, workflows, rights instruments
decisions.rationale: Explicit scope exclusions prevent lifecycle absorption. Creative work (WM-MED-001), media asset (WM-MED-002), publication workflow (WM-ACT-044), parties, identifier agencies, rights instruments, channels, and repositories retain independent mastership. Edition records accountable outcomes without owning decision workflows.

decisions.concept: ISBN/ISSN/DOI target granularity and authority semantics
decisions.rationale: Model acknowledges that ISBN distinguishes product forms, ISSN identifies medium-specific continuing resources, and DOI targets vary by registration policy. It correctly rejects identifier-as-universal-edition-identity but specialist identifier-agency review is required to validate target-granularity mappings across SRC-012, SRC-013, SRC-014.

EPUB Accessibility 1.1 (SRC-018) and Schema.org accessibility properties (SRC-009) are source-grounded. Model qualifies certifier, method, target, and hazard but accessibility-domain specialist review is required to validate conformance interpretation and remediation claims.

decisions.concept: Legal deposit, retraction duties, and jurisdictional profiles
decisions.rationale: Model acknowledges jurisdiction-specific publication, deposit, embargo, retraction, and takedown duties without claiming universality. Book, serial, scholarly, news, legal, and standards publication profiles require sector-specialist and legal review. Known omissions explicitly defer jurisdictional enforcement.

decisions.concept: High confidence claim in single-provider mode
decisions.rationale: Only Codex reviewed this model. Claude timed out on bounded attempts (1800s, 900s, 600s, 300s Sonnet and Haiku). Grok was owner-authorized waived. No independent adversarial provider challenged the 24-finding, 96-question scope, aggregate boundary, or source integration. High confidence is impossible without external review.

decisions.concept: Temporal clock separation for publication lifecycle
decisions.rationale: Model maintains distinct creation, expression, publication, release, online-availability, copyright, deposit, metadata-registration, correction, retraction, and withdrawal timestamps per RFC 3339 (SRC-023). Refuses conflation of publication date, copyright date, availability date, and metadata-creation date across MARC, MODS, BIBFRAME, DataCite, and Crossref.

decisions.concept: Standards crosswalk round-trip loss and version pinning
decisions.rationale: Model declares that IFLA/RDA/BIBFRAME/MARC/MODS/ISBD/DC/Schema.org/ONIX/JATS/Crossref/DataCite/EPUB/IIIF projections must pin source and target versions and disclose semantic loss. Interoperability testing is required to validate transformation rules, round-trip fidelity, and non-obvious loss patterns.

decisions.concept: Provenance and evidence qualification for bibliographic assertions
decisions.rationale: Every finding, statement, identifier, lifecycle assertion, and rights claim retains source reference, transcription status, actor, agency, method, authority, effective time, and revision lineage per PROV-O (SRC-020) and PREMIS (SRC-019). Model avoids unqualified assertion and conflation of cataloger judgment with publisher authority.

deferred_research: ISBN product-form, ISSN medium-edition, DOI registered-referent target granularity mappings require specialist identifier-agency review to validate authority-scoped semantics and non-equivalence claims across SRC-012, SRC-013, SRC-014.

EPUB Accessibility 1.1 conformance, W3C WCAG validation, accessibility feature/hazard metadata, and remediation certification claims require accessibility-domain specialist review beyond static SRC-017, SRC-018 source mapping.

Legal deposit, mandatory publication, retraction duties, embargo enforcement, takedown compliance, and jurisdictional profiles (copyright, moral rights, privacy, consumer protection) require legal specialist review and sector-specific profiling (library, book trade, scholarly, news, legal, standards, audiovisual).

IFLA LRM / RDA / BIBFRAME / MARC / MODS / ISBD / Dublin Core / Schema.org / ONIX / JATS / Crossref / DataCite / EPUB / IIIF crosswalk transformation rules, round-trip fidelity, semantic loss patterns, and version-pinned compatibility matrices require interoperability implementation testing.

Series continuity, numbering irregularity, chronology ambiguity, predecessor/successor changes, ISSN-L linking, medium-split handling, and frequency-change semantics across PRESSoo (SRC-002), MARC holdings, and ISSN guidance require serials-specialist review.

Silent replacement, version-of-record semantics, Crossmark updates, correction notice standards, retraction taxonomy, withdrawal vs tombstone, and post-publication integrity across scholarly, news, legal, and standards sectors require publishing-integrity specialist review.
